hints: Find the time when the particle comes to instantaneous rest at $P$ by setting $v = 0$.
Evaluate $s(5) - s(0)$ to show the distance is $6.25\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
Find the time when the particle comes to rest at point $P$:
Set velocity equal to zero:
$$v(t) = 0.6t^2 - 0.12t^3 = 0$$
Factor out $0.12t^2$:
$$0.12t^2(5 - t) = 0$$
The root $t = 0$ corresponds to the start from rest at $O$, so the time at point $P$ is:
$$t = 5\text{ s}$$

Integrate the velocity function to obtain displacement $s(t)$:
$$s(t) = \int v(t)\,dt = \int \left(0.6t^2 - 0.12t^3\right) dt$$
$$s(t) = 0.6 \times \frac{t^3}{3} - 0.12 \times \frac{t^4}{4} + C = 0.2t^3 - 0.03t^4 + C$$
Since the particle starts from $O$ at $t = 0$, $s(0) = 0 \implies C = 0$:
$$s(t) = 0.2t^3 - 0.03t^4$$

Evaluate the definite distance $OP = s(5)$:
$$s(5) = 0.2 \times 5^3 - 0.03 \times 5^4$$
Compute powers of $5$:
$$5^3 = 125, \quad 5^4 = 625$$
$$0.2 \times 125 = 25$$
$$0.03 \times 625 = 18.75$$
$$OP = 25 - 18.75 = 6.25\text{ m}$$

hints: By continuity of displacement at $t = 5\text{ s}$, $s(5) = 6.25\text{ m}$, so $k(5^3) + c(5^5) = 6.25$.
Differentiate $s = kt^3 + ct^5$ with respect to $t$ to find the velocity: $v = 3kt^2 + 5ct^4$.
Use the given velocity condition $v(5) = 1.25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to set up a second equation: $75k + 3125c = 1.25$.
Subtract the two equations to eliminate $c$ and solve for $k$ and $c$.
walkthrough:
Establish the first equation from continuity of position:
At $t = 5\text{ s}$, the particle is at distance $6.25\text{ m}$ from $O$:
$$s(5) = 6.25$$
$$k \times 5^3 + c \times 5^5 = 6.25$$
$$125k + 3125c = 6.25 \quad \text{[Equation 1]}$$

Differentiate $s(t)$ to derive the velocity expression:
$$v(t) = \frac{ds}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(kt^3 + ct^5\right) = 3kt^2 + 5ct^4$$

Substitute the boundary velocity condition $v(5) = 1.25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$3k(5^2) + 5c(5^4) = 1.25$$
$$3k(25) + 5c(625) = 1.25$$
$$75k + 3125c = 1.25 \quad \text{[Equation 2]}$$

Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 1 to eliminate the $c$ term:
$$(125k + 3125c) - (75k + 3125c) = 6.25 - 1.25$$
$$50k = 5$$
Divide by $50$:
$$k = \frac{5}{50} = 0.1$$

hints: Differentiate the velocity function $v = 3kt^2 + 5ct^4$ with respect to $t$ to find acceleration: $a = 6kt + 20ct^3$.
Substitute $k = 0.1$ and $c = -0.002$ into the acceleration expression: $a = 0.6t - 0.04t^3$.
walkthrough:
State the formula for acceleration as the time derivative of velocity:
$$a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt}$$
With $v(t) = 3kt^2 + 5ct^4$:
$$a(t) = \frac{d}{dt}\left(3kt^2 + 5ct^4\right) = 6kt + 20ct^3$$

Substitute the values $k = 0.1$ and $c = -0.002$ obtained in part (ii):
$$a(t) = 6(0.1)t + 20(-0.002)t^3 = 0.6t - 0.04t^3$$
